item.title: How Do Europe's Companies Regain Their Edge?
item.description: Europe's industrial companies are under growing pressure from high energy and labor costs, weakening investment and intensifying global competition. McKinsey research finds that 45% of European industrial companies are showing signs of financial stress or distress but argues that the decline is not inevitable. Tunde Olanrewaju, Managing Partner for Europe at McKinsey & Company, joins Bloomberg Radio's Ben Boulos and Charles Capel to discuss what is driving Europe's industrial competitiveness challenge and the turnaround strategies that could help companies fight back. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Selloff Rolls On as AI Worries Persist
item.description:
A global selloff in technology stocks is showing no sign of letting up as questions about the outlook for artificial intelligence pile up, with investors turning to bonds for safety. While technology stocks underperformed in Europe, the region’s greater exposure to defensive and cyclical stocks pushed the Stoxx 600 higher.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: China Hits Back at New Trump Tariff Prospects
item.description:
China called the prospect of new US tariffs on its exports “political maneuvering” and said the two nations should work together to maintain their trade truce.
Jensen Huang struck a somber tone a day after his reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, apologizing to employees during an all-hands meeting and sharing that he’d been in daily therapy to address the behavior that led to his brief ouster from the top job.
A global selloff in technology stocks is showing no sign of letting up as questions about the outlook for the artificial intelligence trade pile up.
Today’s guests: Christian Mueller-Glissman, Goldman Sachs Head of Asset Allocation Research; Xiaolan Fu, Oxford University Technology & International Development Professor & Centre of Technology and Industrialisation for Development Founding Director; Caitlin Egen, Control Risks Digital Risks Director. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: ING Sees ‘Full Unwind’ in Emerging-Market Currencies Underway
item.description: Emerging-market currencies face mounting pressure from the technology selloff, the risk of shrinking interest rate premiums and the threat of fresh global tariffs, according to strategists at ING Bank.
item.dc:creator: Andras Gergely

item.title: Dangote Hires Veteran Oil Trader Jonathan Zarembok From Equinor
item.description: Veteran oil trader Jonathan Zarembok is joining Dangote Group, which has a huge refinery in Nigeria and is expanding elsewhere in Africa, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Osae-Brown, Jack Wittels, Serene Cheong and Sherry Su

item.title: Deutsche Bank Is Among Biggest S&P 500 Bulls With 9,000 Target
item.description: Deutsche Bank AG’s Binky Chadha is among the most bullish stock forecasters on Wall Street, predicting the S&P 500 will recover from its rout to rally 25% by the end of next year.
item.dc:creator: Marton Kasnyik

item.title: Aareal Bank Nears Commercial Real Estate SRT With 12% Premium
item.description: Aareal Bank AG is set to pay investors a premium of more than 12% to hedge part of the risk on a commercial real estate lending book worth around €2.5 billion ($2.7 billion) in only its second such deal.
item.dc:creator: Esteban Duarte

item.title: US Tech Stocks Set to Extend Declines on Lingering AI Worries
item.description: US technology stocks were set to decline for a second day as investors worried about the payoff from hefty investments in the artificial intelligence buildout.
item.dc:creator: Rose Henderson

item.title: AUD/USD: Aussie Set for Biggest Monthly Drop in Four Years as Stocks Fall
item.description: The Australian dollar is poised for its biggest monthly slide in more than 13 years as it extended losses on Wednesday, with the weakness in global stocks damping demand for currencies linked to growth.
item.dc:creator: Masaki Kondo and Ruth Carson

item.title: EasyJet Profit Hit By Iran War as Apollo Takeover Looms
item.description: EasyJet Plc said the fallout from Middle East war eroded most of its profit in the fiscal year, with soaring fuel prices hitting the budget carrier as it prepares to be taken over by a US private equity firm early next year.
item.dc:creator: Kate Duffy

item.title: Danantara Reports $634 Billion Assets in Audited Accounts
item.description: Indonesia’s Danantara reported about $634 billion in consolidated assets at the end of 2025 in its first audited accounts, well below the roughly $1 trillion officials have often cited for the state investment agency central to President Prabowo Subianto’s overhaul of government-owned companies in Southeast Asia’s largest economy.
item.dc:creator: Grace Sihombing and Harry Suhartono

item.title: Treasury Rally Picks Up as Stock Selloff Dents Risk Appetite
item.description: Treasuries rallied across the curve on Wednesday as renewed losses in technology shares dented investor appetite for risk assets.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Carson

item.title: Market Convulsions Create a $385 Billion Winner: India
item.description: Indian stocks extended their world-beating November rally and the rupee hit an eight-month high versus the dollar as renewed selling in the artificial intelligence trade spurred demand for the nation’s assets.
item.dc:creator: Samie Modak and Subhadip Sircar

item.title: Metals Rout Deepens as AI, Fed Worries Fuel Bearish Sentiment
item.description: Copper, aluminum and tin all added to Tuesday’s sharp selloff in metals as tech stocks extended losses and traders braced for US inflation data that will feed the Federal Reserve’s next moves on interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Gold Slumps Below $3,500 an Ounce To Lowest in More Than a Year
item.description: Gold tumbled below $3,500 an ounce to its lowest point in more than a year, as a selloff in stocks continued and investors waited for a key inflation print that could shape expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ryan and Wendy Wells

item.title: Advent Weighs Takeover Of Testing Firm Bureau Veritas
item.description: Advent is considering a bid to acquire French testing firm Bureau Veritas SA, people with knowledge of the matter said, in what would be one of the largest buyouts of a European company this year.
